ssh_notes: Instance 37134508 on ssh3.vast.ai:14508 (public IP 222.230.13.166, Japan JP, machine_id 31089 host_id 45726). The Vast.ai SSH proxy auto-attaches a tmux session on TTY logins -- this is disabled for this instance via 'touch /root/.no_auto_tmux' built into the create-instance --onstart-cmd. After that, non-TTY 'ssh -i /c/Users/md1avn/.ssh/id_ed25519 -p 14508 root@ssh3.vast.ai <cmd>' works for stdin-piped commands and run_with_logs wrappers. SSH key on this Windows host is at /c/Users/md1avn/.ssh/id_ed25519 (NOT ~/.ssh/id_ed25519 because '~' resolves to U:/ which is an unmounted network drive). For Vast.ai key attachment: registered TWO SSH key entries with identical key material -- id 855344 (clean comment 'md1avn-t0113') was added during t0113 setup and id 856172 (clean comment 'md1avn-t0114') was added during this task's setup via 'vastai attach ssh 37134508'. Both work. The legacy id 801863 with comment 'shefuniad\md1avn@TEN00BE4360B45A' is NOT used because the literal backslash in the comment field corrupts key parsing on the Vast.ai SSH proxy (root cause of t0113's setup-time SSH failure 660-second delay). The onstart-cmd injects the clean key comment 'md1avn-t0114' into /root/.ssh/authorized_keys directly so SSH auth succeeds on the first attempt regardless of Vast.ai key-attach state. PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8 and PYTHONUTF8=1 must be set in the local shell when running pip/ssh commands wrapped in run_with_logs; otherwise run_with_logs.py crashes on non-UTF-8 output from the remote. Note the cosmetic 'Welcome to vast.ai' banner is appended to every command's stderr by the Vast.ai login wrapper -- treat as benign. The Vast.ai create-instance API call returned empty stdout (exit 0) for this offer; the instance appeared in 'vastai show instances' within 10s so there was no phantom-instance retry (unlike t0113 which had to clean up a phantom 37106446).

mod_compile.note_on_load_mechanisms: Modern NEURON places libnrnmech.so directly in x86_64/ (not in x86_64/.libs/ as older versions did). 'load_mechanisms(x86_64)' from Python returns False because it looks for the legacy path, but hasattr(h, 'bkt80') etc. all return True because NEURON auto-loads x86_64/libnrnmech.so from CWD on import. This matches t0112's and t0113's observation exactly. Library size 118704 bytes matches t0113's library size exactly (same Linux ABI, same Zen-3 Milan target, same NEURON 8.2.7 build).
